Subject: ACT NOW - 2013 TAX-WISE GIVING 
Date: Tue, 08 Oct 2013 14:42:45 +0000 
Dear Jeffrey, 
Thank you for your support of AJC. It's that time of the year when you may be 
considering your charitable contributions. You have until December 31, 2013 to 
use the IRA charitable rollover provision to make a gift to AJC, and receive tax 
benefits. Click here to learn how now! 
Who can take advantage of the IRA charitable rollover? What is the maximum gift? 
If you have an IRA, and you and/or your spouse are 70'/: and older, you each can make a 
tax-free charitable distribution of up to $100,000 from your IRAs directly to a public 
charity, such as AJC, through December 31, 2013. 
What are the Benefits? 
Your IRA charitable rollover transfer to AJC counts towards your minimum required annual 
withdrawal from your IRA. By taking advantage of this opportunity, the funds you 
transfer to AJC will not be included in your taxable income. In some cases, lowering your 
taxable income may place you in a more favorable tax bracket, and using IRA assets for the 
charitable rollover can also reduce your taxable estate. 
Please note that while your taxable income will be lowered, the distribution to AJC will not 
be eligible for a charitable tax deduction. 
Individual financial and estate planning objectives vary. Please consult with your tax professional. To 
learn more about making IRA charitable rollover contributions, please click here or for questions, 
please contact Debra Rubenstein, AM National Director of Planned Giving, at (877) 252-2040, or by 
email at plannedgiving@ajc.org.

Dear Tenants, 
Beginning Friday night at lOpm, the building will be demolishing the floor tile in and around the low rise elevator bank. Therefore, the 
Lexington Avenue entrance will be closed between the hours of lOpm and 2am. All persons will be required to enter and exit through the

• Special Orders: We are able to offer our best discounts to customers who order in bulk. We determine our pricing on a project-by-project basis. 
Depending on the product and quantity you require, our special order pricing can be anywhere front a 300400% discount. Our lead-time for special 
orders is approximately 120 days. 
• Express Ship: While our RH Contract lead time for delivering most special order products is 120 days, we realize that RH Contract customers need 
products more urgently for certain projects. We have a core range of Express Ship products in stock at all times that can be delivered to your project 
within 1-2 weeks. Our quick-ship products are typically offered at a 25-40% discount. 
• Con Inventory: The Contract discount is also available for our core inventory of product. The minimum discount that will be offered to Contract 
customers is 20%.

Subject: JE's Preferred Protocol for Announcing Guests When with Guests 
Date: Sun, 22 Sep 2013 16:47:23 +0000 
Importance: High 
Lesley, 
Please cut and paste and forward this message below to all who may announce guests to JE. (Jo Jo walked ahead 
of me today with a new a guest and opened the dining room door when JE was at table with guests before I 
could stop him (I did not want to shout at Jo Jo). JE did not like this. So we need to distribute this to everyone 
who may announce guests requiring an email acknowledgement that it was received please. I will acquire all 
emails of those I need Monday from you so I can do this in the future. Thank you for your assistance this time. 
Mark 
Protocol to Announce Additional Arriving Guest to JE When the Dining Room Door is Closed 
If JE is seated with guests in the dining room and the dining room door is closed: 
I. Do not open the door to announce other expected or unexpected guest. 
2. Write down clearly in print on a piece of paper that the guest (with his/her name) has arrived, place it on a 
small serving tray, and deliver it quietly to JE's right hand side via the right pantry entry with two doors (in 
between discussions with his guest at table if possible). 
3. Wait silently for a response standing slightly in back of him to his right side in his view with your hands by 
your side. 
4. Upon receiving JE's response exit quietly back through the same pantry with two doors and let the guests 
know to follow you in through the dining room door or how long it will be until JE will see them. 
5. Make certain if the guest has to wait to ask if he/she would like anything. 
6. Make certain the guest is checked on regularly (at least every ten minutes) thereafter if he/she has to wait. 
Best regards, 
Mark Tollison
